g1.label: 1 — for more than ___ years
g1.why: The text says Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples cared for the land for more than 60,000 years.

g2.label: 2 — after ___, when the British arrived
g2.why: The text says the British arrived after 1788.

g3.label: 3 — the constitution did not ___
g3.why: The text says until 1967 the constitution did not even count Aboriginal people.

g4.label: 4 — voted ___ to change that
g4.why: The text says more than 90 per cent of Australians voted 'yes' in the 1967 referendum.

g5.label: 5 — recognised ___ title
g5.why: The text says the High Court recognised native title in the famous Mabo decision.

g6.label: 6 — the ___ said sorry
g6.why: The text says the prime minister said sorry to the Stolen Generations in 2008.

g7.label: 7 — children who had been ___ from their families
g7.why: The Stolen Generations were Aboriginal children taken from their families.

g8.label: 8 — Aboriginal culture ___ in art and music
g8.why: The text says Aboriginal culture is celebrated in art, music and festivals.

g1.label: 1 — Aboriginal people ___ the right to vote
g1.why: Two-object passive: the receiver becomes the subject — plural 'were given'.

g2.label: 2 — their land ___ back
g2.why: The land (singular) receives the action — 'was handed back'.

g3.label: 3 — the Stolen Generations ___ an apology
g3.why: The receiver becomes the subject — plural past passive 'were offered'.

g4.label: 4 — visitors ___ the story
g4.why: A general present situation; visitors receive the action — 'are shown'.

g5.label: 5 — children ___ English
g5.why: Past passive with the receiver as subject — 'were taught'.

g6.label: 6 — maps ___ to every visitor
g6.why: The thing becomes the subject; the receiver follows 'to' — 'are given'.

g7.label: 7 — ___ for the land for thousands of years (review)
g7.why: Review from 'Into the Red Centre': 'by the time' + duration before a past event needs the past perfect.

g8.label: 8 — the didgeridoo ___ last night (review)
g8.why: Review from 'Just Me and My Backpack': 'last night' + a received action — simple past passive.

g1.correct: Aboriginal people were given the right to vote in 1962
accept: Aboriginal people were given the right to vote in 1962
g1.label: 1 — gave Aboriginal people the right
g1.why: Person as subject: was/were + past participle; the thing (the right) stays after it.

g2.correct: The Meriam people were handed back their land in 1992
accept: The Meriam people were handed back their land in 1992
The Meriam people were handed their land back in 1992
g2.label: 2 — handed the Meriam people back their land
g2.why: Two-object passive with a phrasal verb: the person becomes the subject; 'back' stays after the verb.

g3.correct: The Stolen Generations were offered a formal apology in 2008
accept: The Stolen Generations were offered a formal apology in 2008
g3.label: 3 — offered the Stolen Generations an apology
g3.why: The receiver becomes the subject; the verb keeps both objects in the passive.

g4.correct: Visitors are shown sacred rock paintings
accept: Visitors are shown sacred rock paintings
Sacred rock paintings are shown to visitors
g4.label: 4 — shows visitors sacred paintings
g4.why: General truth → present passive with the receiver as subject ('Sacred rock paintings are shown to visitors' also fits).

g5.correct: The children were taught English at the mission school
accept: The children were taught English at the mission school
g5.label: 5 — taught the children English
g5.why: Past passive with the receiver as subject; the second object (English) remains.

g6.correct: Young artists will be given a grant next year
accept: Young artists will be given a grant next year
Young artists will be given a grant for their paintings
g6.label: 6 — will give young artists a grant
g6.why: Future passive: will be + past participle.

g7.correct: We were told the story of the Rainbow Serpent
accept: We were told the story of the Rainbow Serpent
The story of the Rainbow Serpent was told to us
g7.label: 7 — told us the story of the Rainbow Serpent
g7.why: Past passive with the person as subject — or 'The story of the Rainbow Serpent was told to us'.
